newsitem.title: GREECE: Greek bonds stable in volatile trade, ecu/drs flat.
newsitem.headline: Greek bonds stable in volatile trade, ecu/drs flat.

text.p: Greek interbank depos and forex forwards were little changed in late dealings and bonds settled around morning levels in a volatile session that saw prices first rise and then fall by about 30 basis points, dealers said.
The drachma was locked in the 308.20/45 range, hovering around 308.35/30 in late unexcited trade, forex dealers said.

"Five- and seven-year coupon bond prices went up 30 basis points in light volume today before reversing course to settle around morning levels," said a dealer at a private bank. "It was a volatile session."
Dealers cited the high cost of carry, tight liquidity conditions, the lack of a broad based pool of end-investors, and concerns about a rise in German rates for the weak demand of coupon bonds.
The finance ministry set the first annual coupon of FRNs to be auctioned on August 21 at 10.30 percent based on the ongoing 12-month T-bill rate of 9.50 percent plus a spread of 80 basis.
Greece will auction 100 billion drachmas of seven-year floaters on August 21 and offer 12-month T-bills to the public at 9.50 percent on Wednesday.
The treasury slashed three-, six- and 12-month T-bill rates by 10 basis points to 8.4 percent, 8.7 percent and 9.5 percent effective today.
The 10-year bond was trading around 94.75 at mid-session, with the spread over Bunds standing at 404 basis points.
The market was quoted at 156.60/70 from Tuesday's 156.635 fix, the dollar at 287.14/24 from 287.660 and the ecu at 308.15/25 from 308.290.
"Ecu/drachma was set at 308.290 in today's fixing but the central bank opened it at 308.18, again showing its determination to stick to its hard drachma policy," said a forex dealer.
